subject: Qualification brief: model choices, perf evidence & next steps for Synthara pilot
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 15:04:00 +0000
Subject: Qualification brief: model choices, perf evidence & next steps for Synthara pilot

Hi Emma — thanks again for a great discovery call today. Below is a concise post-call qualification brief and recommended next steps so we can get you into a short, measurable pilot ASAP. I pulled Redwood-verified perf profiles and a minimal prompt set you can use to reproduce the signals we discussed.

1) Summary of fit (short):
- Target workload: high-throughput question-answering (search/assistant mix) with 512 token average responses and occasional long-form (1k tokens) fallbacks.
- Constraints: p95 latency target <= 350ms for interactive queries, burst TPS up to 60 req/s, and strict PII redaction requirement.

2) Recommended candidate models (prioritized):
- Redwood-7B-quant-v2 (cost-friendly; strong throughput). Verified TPS: 1800 token/s on a 4-GPU serving pool; p50=38ms, p95=210ms, p99=430ms (512 tokens). Link: https://redwood.ai/perf/profiles/redwood-7b-quant-v2
- Redwood-13B-int8-latency-optimized (balanced quality/latency; fallback for longer context). Verified TPS: 950 token/s; p50=72ms, p95=320ms, p99=610ms (1k tokens). Link: https://redwood.ai/perf/profiles/redwood-13b-int8-latency-optimized
- OpenOrchid-13B-fp16 (higher quality for edge-case extraction; higher cost). Local perf snapshot attached in the dashboard link below.

3) Known quality/regression notes:
- Redwood-7B quantized builds can show occasional edge-case hallucination on long numeric tables — we recommend prompt templates with explicit schema enforcement (examples attached).
- For extraction tasks, the 13B variants show better entity recall but at ~1.8x token-cost. We should run a 24-hour regression sweep against your top 200 production prompts (we can reuse the attached prompt_set_v1.json).

4) Evidence & artifacts we shared:
- Benchmark dashboard (latency/TPS traces, p50/p95/p99): https://redwood-internal.drive/synthara/benchmarks/20270914-dashboard
- Perf profiles: links above.
- Prompt pack for first-pass regression tests: attached synthara_prompt_set_v1.json
- Minimal pilot MOP (scope, metrics, guardrails): attached synthara_pilot_mop.pdf

5) Proposed next steps (timeboxed):
- A: Confirm pilot scope and legal/ops contacts (your side) — Emma/ops — by EOD Fri
- B: Redwood to spin a 2-week pilot environment (dedicated capacity) and run the 24-hr regression sweep on your top 200 prompts — kickoff once scope confirmed (target start: next Tue)
- C: Quick enablement: 45-minute tech sync (Marissa + Ben) to align telemetry and guardrails.

Ask: can you confirm the pilot scope and the ops person we should loop in? If yes, I’ll send a calendar invite for the tech sync and provision the pilot pool.

Thanks —
Aditya Rao
Enterprise Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0104

Emma/Aditya — quick tech note from the infra side before we kick off provisioning.

- Burst behavior: the verified profiles assume the serving pool is configured with the autoscale burst option enabled (we pre-warm KV caches and allow 2x short-duration burst capacity). Under a sustained 2x burst (120 req/s sustained for >60s) you will see p95 move toward ~480-650ms on the 7B quant build due to GPU scheduling and KV-cache churn. The 13B-int8-latency-optimized profile sustains spikes better at the cost of higher token cost.
- Guardrails to recommend before live: request-level token cap (1,500 tokens), KV-prefill for hot prefixes, and prefix-based caching for repetitive user queries. We can include these in the pilot MOP.
- Telemetry hooks we need from your side: request_id, user_id (hashed), route tag. If you can provide access to a short-lived S3 bucket or grant our pilot service role, we can push traces into the dashboard link.

I’ll bring a short checklist to the tech sync outlining the minimal ops IAM and network requirements.

—Marissa
